changesVerified.finding: DecreaseKey now throws ArgumentException when newPriority is not strictly smaller than the current stored priority, before mutating state or sifting. The accompanying prose explains why the guard is load-bearing rather than defensive filler: SiftUp only ever moves a node toward the root, so a larger-or-equal priority would silently break the heap property with 'nothing to signal it went wrong,' and the prose correctly attributes the same check to CLRS's DECREASE-KEY. The worked example in the same block only ever calls DecreaseKey with a strictly smaller value (5 -> 0), so the guard doesn't fire and the printed output (0: compact-index / 2: send-digest / 5: backup) still hand-verifies against the trace. This is a correctness fix presented as one, not dressed up as a bigger feature than it is -- no scope inflation, no invented benchmark, no ad-adjacent framing.
